players.product: utility T&D grid infrastructure (transmission/substation connectors and hardware up to 765 kV, System Control control houses) and data-center electrical components (Burndy connectors, PCX power skids, 800 V pin & sleeve devices)

quarterly_data.signal: Q4 2025 results (CFO): 'Net sales of $1.493 billion in 2025 increased by 12% as compared to the prior year, driven by 9% organic growth and acquisitions contributing 3%'; Electrical Solutions and Grid Infrastructure both delivered double-digit organic growth, 'an acceleration versus prior quarters driven by incremental price realization and stronger demand in data center and utility T&D markets'. Adjusted operating profit of $349 million (up 19%) with 140 basis points of adjusted operating margin expansion; adjusted diluted EPS of $4.73, up 15%; Q4 free cash flow of $389 million and full-year 2025 free cash flow of $875 million (90% conversion on adjusted net income).
quarterly_data.figure: Q4 net sales $1.493 billion (+12%; 9% organic growth); adjusted operating profit $349 million (+19%); adj. EPS $4.73 (+15%); full-year 2025 free cash flow $875 million

quarterly_data.signal: Utility Solutions (CFO): Q4 net sales of $936 million grew 10% (organic 7%, acquisitions 4%). Grid infrastructure, about three-quarters of segment sales, 'was up 12% organically', with 'strong growth across distribution, substation, and transmission markets' as 'Utility customers continue to aggressively invest in new transmission and substation infrastructure to interconnect new sources of load and generation on the grid'. Grid automation sales were down 8% on weaker new project activity in meters and AMI (CEO: that business is 'really at the bottom', with book-to-bill 'at one or close to one'). Segment adjusted operating profit was $235 million, up 20%, with margins up 200 basis points. Management also said over 80% of the segment portfolio is aligned to electric T&D components and solutions, and transmission and substation grew double digits for full-year 2025.
quarterly_data.figure: Utility Solutions Q4 net sales $936 million (+10%; organic 7%); grid infrastructure up 12% organically; grid automation down 8%; adjusted operating profit $235 million (+20%); over 80% of the segment portfolio aligned to electric T&D

quarterly_data.signal: Data center, Q4 2025: Electrical Solutions organic growth of 13% was 'driven by significant strength in data center markets'; 'Data center growth exceeded 60% in the quarter', helped by 'targeted capacity investments in our balance of systems components as well as strong project activity in our modular power distribution skid'. CFO: 'I think that was roughly 40% growth for the full year in data center', and the fourth quarter 'was pretty heavy with data center projects'. Electrical Solutions Q4 adjusted operating profit was $114 million (up 18%); full-year 2025 adjusted operating margins in the segment reached 20% for the first time.
quarterly_data.figure: Electrical Solutions Q4 net sales $557 million (organic growth 13%); data center growth exceeded 60% in Q4; roughly 40% growth for the full year in data center; adjusted operating profit $114 million (+18%)

quarterly_data.signal: Initial 2026 outlook (CFO): 'we are initiating our 2026 outlook this morning for 7% to 9% total sales growth, $19.15 to $19.85 of adjusted earnings per share, and approximately 90% free cash flow conversion on adjusted net income'. Organic growth of 5% to 7% across the portfolio (Utility Solutions 5% to 7%, Electrical Solutions 4% to 6%), with about 10% adjusted operating profit growth at the midpoint, including wraparound contribution from the DMC Power acquisition. Margin expansion is expected in both segments; the CFO called an analyst's estimate of the implied margin expansion 'about right'. On cash, the CFO confirmed an analyst's free-cash-flow range: 'You're right that we're thinking about $900 to $1 billion of free cash flow next year'.
quarterly_data.figure: FY2026 outlook (initial): 7% to 9% total sales growth; 5% to 7% organic growth (Utility Solutions 5% to 7%, Electrical Solutions 4% to 6%); adj. EPS $19.15 to $19.85; approximately 90% free cash flow conversion

quarterly_data.signal: Data center outlook for 2026: 'we expect growth to be led by data center markets, which now represent more than 10% of segment sales and are expected to expand mid-teens' (Electrical Solutions). CFO: data center growth comes from two places. The first is the modular power distribution skid business, which 'had a pretty heavy project load throughout 2025' and is 'anticipated to continue a heavy project load in 2026', so its growth rate 'will step down a little bit'. The second is connectors and grounding products, which 'continue to grow nicely'. He added 'we're looking at that, you know, mid to high teens on our outlook for data center on the electrical side' and 'we have good line of sight, to data center projects throughout the duration of 2026'. CEO: much of the business is short cycle (Burndy connectors), and 'we're adding capital. We're expanding. And if that proves out to be conservative, we'll do better this year.'
quarterly_data.figure: data center more than 10% of Electrical Solutions segment sales; FY2026 data center growth outlook mid-teens (mid to high teens on the electrical side)

quarterly_data.signal: T&D orders and the substation outlook (CEO): 'we started to see this inflection in our order book in, like, the September time frame and particularly in the areas of T&D and data center'. Q4 organic growth came from new orders rather than from working down backlog, and 'we've even built a little bit of backlog at some of our businesses like the T&D business'; 'That order momentum going into '26 has continued'. Hubbell is 'primarily a book-to-bill business', though it has 'a few businesses where we're fully filled with backlog'. Transmission and substation have been 'growing in these high single, low double digits for a while'; for 2026, 'think about the substation and transmission in the kind of high single digits and distribution. Mid-single digits'. Substation demand is 'clearly aided by data centers right now': 'A data center will be, you know, putting up the infrastructure and then put the substation right next to it'. The Systems Control and DMC acquisitions are 'very much in that space'. On large transmission projects running into '26 and '27, he said 'We very much participate in it.'
quarterly_data.figure: 2026 view: substation and transmission high single digits, distribution mid-single digits; order inflection in the September time frame

quarterly_data.signal: Capacity and automation for data-center connectors (CFO): Burndy (electrical connectors and grounding) has 'strong specified positions with major customers' in data center markets. After 'the significant demand inflection we've experienced in high-growth verticals like data center', Hubbell used capacity expansion investments to automate production, including 'four specialized enclosed automation work cells for copper lug production'. The cells combine 'six manual production processes into single-flow automated lines for high-running SKUs, reducing factory processing time from days to minutes for certain product lines', which let the company 'increase output to serve strong customer demand'. CEO: 'CapEx continued to be highest return project followed by acquisitions'.
quarterly_data.figure: four specialized enclosed automation work cells for copper lug production; six manual production processes combined into single-flow automated lines

quarterly_data.signal: Pricing, cost inflation and tariffs (CFO): incremental price actions were implemented in Q4, and the previously anticipated 'about three points of price for the full year' 2025 is 'consistent with what we saw come through'; 2026 carries wraparound price plus 'modest incremental price to start the year'. 'we did see some creep coming out of the fourth quarter with higher copper, aluminum, steel' and 'we're anticipating about mid-single digits for cost inflation in 2026', which price and productivity are meant to offset (price-cost productivity 'neutral to positive'). About half of the cost pool is materials (metals and components). On tariffs: 'we saw about $150 million worth of tariff and related, you know, cost' in 2025, managed a little lower during the year, with few recent changes in tariff rates.
quarterly_data.figure: about three points of price in 2025; about mid-single digits cost inflation expected in 2026; about $150 million worth of tariff and related cost in 2025

quarterly_data.signal: DMC Power and M&A (CFO): DMC Power, a substation business, was part of Hubbell for basically all of Q4, with sales and margin 'right in line with our expectations'. 'our outlook contemplates $130 million of revenue and roughly 40% operating margins, which is net of integration costs'. 2025 M&A was 'three deals that roughly $950 million deployed'. CEO: the acquisition pipeline 'has bolt-ons in it' and 'some larger deals', focused on T&D and core electrical markets.
quarterly_data.figure: DMC Power 2026 outlook: $130 million of revenue and roughly 40% operating margins; three deals with roughly $950 million deployed in 2025
